result.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?
result.markdown:
For most small teams, I'd recommend **1Password** as the best overall password manager.

If keeping costs down is the priority, **Bitwarden** is my alternative and arguably the best value.

The important thing is to choose a business plan, not simply have everyone use individual password manager accounts. You want shared vaults, centralised administration and the ability to revoke access immediately when someone leaves.

## My top 4 recommendations

![1Password 8.12 - TidBITS](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/34HDvvYhqgd6AnMFmrlTm3hAXFxcbeGEwY_LB_XZ_XGVtrk4a2QxTEX-2LBZt2GGXhIIaKEolAWfkyjqt2bzeCs60tKyMvcGjArpm-vdyy1ZPxujq2f9_l2uItYJrXcwCcU9bPBSy8AGv_Ou2YF6Ce5xYeilxXBZ8f7ED4T1F4V2OwIPdBn46M8zBrxXTO4w?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. 1Password**

(Best overall)

- Excellent, intuitive interface.
- Shared vaults for departments and projects.
- Granular permissions and access controls.
- Strong admin tools and security reporting.
- Good for non-technical employees.

**Best if\:** You want something polished that employees will actually enjoy using.

Business: approximately \$8.99/user/month; Starter Pack also available for 10 users.

[1Password business](https://1password.com/business)

---

![Test Bitwarden Premium - Gestionnaire de mots de passe - Que Choisir Ensemble](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/hC5M3yQmIFKAAlHcnKpChWSt35-xr8mlIVRywSu-o8DpkerDwLMFxvrII2QFuvOsSP0k6Fo_mQuwr7t8sXrBNPDXf_LEbep8cD4z2PlCIIwWjH4OqBMrEZ0-9cp7BChiCyWOBI7Pq7evrJY8TBbAUMof-Y5H7s49GfDyBJKLiGrh0gHLhDv6TMbIv6ti_DVz?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Bitwarden**

(Best value)

- Open-source core.
- Shared collections and team vaults.
- Admin console and audit/event logs.
- Good security and access management.
- Self-hosting options.

**Best if\:** You want strong functionality without spending too much.

Teams: approximately \$4/user/month, billed annually.

[Bitwarden business](https://bitwarden.com/business/)

---

![Keeper Security Logo PNG,  Vector (AI, EPS, CDR, PDF, SVG) - iconLogoVector](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/hjZLLtGaZjkKvsDiCoIrNA749yx3vMYIFoRmmV0blB-pAj7O30nu3RJOVVhVRwgAOkJUfJ3datZ7pfH1wp7yeplrEL3FQ-HNOpCzlVOW0OcMr1CFjIFAx50apRkdH6sYOH31WcP6gfXOxeAN8qubYhHhGYA5yXp1bc7wqtCxjN2WEQuyMALTG1Pwne14BXyG?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Keeper**

- Excellent administrative controls.
- Shared folders and team permissions.
- Strong security and compliance features.
- Useful for businesses with more complex requirements.

**Best if\:** Security controls and compliance are particularly important.

[Keeper business](https://www.keepersecurity.com/business.html)

---

![The best password managers in 2025 | Tom's Guide](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/S30I88layvxbkaDwXaWP5XnJ7U511ARCXJEcDjYd8i8QoMbXMBiKKYXroCriJ7kBR0oi7lM-NLlyOXMHqaLP4YKGj6rWlLsTvfSS4pKj24h_up7wZjWKu6xYF8rT-_7bc8XbvU4PlaIDiwcj88cnT8GVhbZrDMRuBptQttvTl2oiFqpoAxV9-pe3un--FrSZ?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Proton Pass**

- Privacy-focused approach.
- Secure sharing.
- Email aliases and password management.
- Attractive lower-cost options.

**Best if\:** Privacy and European data protection considerations are priorities.

[Proton Pass for Business](https://proton.me/business/pass)

These comparisons are based on available 2026 product and pricing information. [toolsandthrive.com](https://toolsandthrive.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.techrepublic.com](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/password-managers-built-teams/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[dupple.com](https://dupple.com/learn/best-password-manager-for-teams?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[vettlo.com](https://vettlo.com/tools/best-password-managers-for-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What I'd look for in a small-team setup

Regardless of which product you choose, I'd consider these essential\:

| Feature | Why it matters |
|--------|--------|
| Shared vaults | Share company credentials securely |
| User permissions | Control who sees which passwords |
| Admin console | Manage the whole team |
| 2FA | Protect accounts against unauthorised access |
| Audit logs | Track access and changes |
| Offboarding | Revoke access when employees leave |
| Secure sharing | Avoid sending passwords through Slack or email |


## My recommendation depends on your team size

I'd narrow it down to two products: 1Password and Bitwarden.

A few questions will help me make a more definitive recommendation\:

**1\. How big is your team?**
